newsitem.title: CANADA: DBRS says upgrades debt ratings for Saskatchewan.
newsitem.headline: DBRS says upgrades debt ratings for Saskatchewan.

text.p: Dominion Bond Rating Service said on Tuesday it uograded its debt ratings for the Canadian province of Saskatchewan to reflect its improving fiscal situation.
The rating agency said long term debt issued and guaranteed by the province was upgraded to A (low) from BBB (high).
Short term debt issued and guaranteed by the province was upgraded to R-1 (low) from R-2 (high).
"The province has demonstrated its commitment to meeting its fiscal objectives...and fully intends to generate continuing budget surpluses over the next few years," DBRS said in a statement.
Other positive factors include continued economic strength, a large natural resource base and a portfolio of investments that could be sold to reduce debt.
However, Saskatchewan remains vulnerable to an economic downturn given its dependence on commodities. Tax levels also remain high, DBRS said.
